card.name: Linking words before adverse-effect terms
card.fires_on: Small linking words or verbs right after a phrase like "may result", "characterized", "may lead" or "exposes users", just before a named adverse condition. Seen in warnings and precautions sections.

modes.label: Result/lead phrases
modes.description: The word in or to after "result", "lead" or "exposes users", introducing a harmful outcome.
modes.example: Concomitant use of Qelbree with an MAOI may lead<< to>> a potentially life-threatening hypertensive crisis.

modes.label: Characterized by
modes.description: The word by after "characterized" when describing a syndrome.
modes.example: Refeeding severely undernourished patients may result in refeeding syndrome, characterized<< by>> the intracellular shift of potassium, phosph

modes.label: Causal verbs after may
modes.description: A verb such as trigger or disrupt right after "may", before the affected condition.
modes.example: In susceptible individuals, volatile anesthetic agents, including desflurane, may<< trigger>> malignant hyperthermia, a skeletal muscle
